_comment: The fork targets Gecko 157+. This file is the machine-checked record of
which platform capabilities the code actually relies on, so a Chromium-
shaped assumption cannot creep back in behind a plausible comment.
capabilities = load-bearing: without it a feature is missing or wrong, and
shipsInFirefox is the floor the target must clear. hostProbes = the code
feature-detects and degrades when the host says no, with `why` naming what
is lost. The split is the point: a probe is not automatically safe, and a
new one has to be argued for rather than inherited.
tests/capabilities.test.mjs enforces it: declared grants must match the
userscript banner exactly, every usedBy/verifiedBy path must exist, no
capability may require a Firefox newer than the 157 floor, anything in
`retired` must not reappear in src/, every capability/hostProbe token must
really appear in the files it claims, and every `probes` chain the code
feature-detects must be classified in exactly one entry - so adopting a
new platform API cannot skip the manifest the way scheduler.postTask and
TextTrack did.

Known boundary of the scan: it reads `typeof` chains whose root is a global or a known host object. A `typeof` probe on a local reference (cue.getCueAsHTML, event.getPredictedEvents) starts at a lowercase local name, and an unguarded bare global (new MediaMetadata) is not a typeof at all - neither is machine-visible. Both are recorded here by hand instead, and the token check keeps those rows honest too. The scan is a floor on coverage, not a ceiling.
or a known host object. A member probe on a local reference (cue.
getCueAsHTML, event.getPredictedEvents) and an
unguarded bare global (new MediaMetadata) are NOT machine-visible; those are
recorded here by hand. The scan is a floor on coverage, not a ceiling.

capabilities.summary: One shared stylesheet, upgraded in place across shadow roots
Frame-clock sampling for the jank watchdog and resume timing
Priority + delay + abort task scheduling behind every deferred path: removal grace, dom-watch defer, lifecycle settle, context retry, resume throttle
capabilities.note: Called unconditionally on the 157 floor, so there is no probe to classify; the jsdom test host gets a timer-backed polyfill from tests/loader.mjs. scheduler.yield is deliberately not used; see the module header.

capabilities.summary: Native WebVTT parsing, cuechange scheduling at exact enter/exit boundaries, and VTTCue.getCueAsHTML() for spec-whitelisted cue markup
capabilities.note: The renderer never parses cue text: getCueAsHTML is why <b>/<i>/<c>/ruby survive as real nodes. 31 covers VTTCue, its geometry, and getCueAsHTML together; region support would be 59.

capabilities.summary: Rich OS media-surface metadata (title, artist, artwork) for the media session
capabilities.note: Constructed unguarded, so this is an implicit dependency: tests/loader.mjs shims MediaMetadata because no test host has it.

grants.why: Manager-scoped storage: readable from any @match origin, unlike a page origin's localStorage.
Cross-tab notification for pf:configs - the one capability the page origin cannot provide.
Detaches the above; a grant without its remover cannot clean up.
Manager-cached stylesheet warm-load, upgraded in place over the embedded sheet.
CORS-bypassing subtitle fetch from user-supplied hosts.

retired.why: Nothing in the fork subscribes to route changes: same-document navigation is out of scope, so there is no consumer to receive the event. Re-granting it would widen the permission surface for zero coverage.
Gecko does not implement LoAF. The rAF frame-gap watchdog in src/shared/diagnostics.js is the debug-only replacement.
Never called by any feature, so the grant would be dead permission surface. Use navigator.clipboard instead.

hostProbes.summary: Is there a document at all?
hostProbes.why: yield_() needs visibilityState to decide between a frame and a task. Node and worker hosts have no document, and both resolve on a MessageChannel task instead.

hostProbes.summary: Frame boundary for yield_() and the jank watchdog
hostProbes.why: Absent on Node/jsdom, where yield_ falls back to a MessageChannel task behind a 50ms backstop, so boot cannot stall on a host that never paints.

hostProbes.summary: Off-screen gate that stops media-clock writes for players the user cannot see
hostProbes.why: Without it the gate stays open, which is the safe direction: saves continue, nothing is lost.

hostProbes.summary: Compact-mode auto-detect and the panel breakpoint listener
hostProbes.why: jsdom has no viewport engine; matches is false, so the shell never auto-switches to compact and no listener fires.

hostProbes.summary: UA-owned Escape watcher for the panel
hostProbes.why: Gecko does not implement it, so the fork's own keydown Escape path is the live one on every target. The branch exists for hosts that do.
hostProbes.note: Documented as absent on the target platform, not merely unimplemented.

hostProbes.why: Heads without a screen object skip the check rather than measuring against a bogus viewport.
A manager that does not provide it simply has no menu; the settings surface carries the same switch.
Missing remover is handled by no-op, so a teardown cannot throw on a manager without it.
Without it resume entries do not sync live between tabs; they still sync on next load.
A grant without its remover is exactly the case that leaks, so the remover is probed too and no-ops.
Absent, the injected stylesheet is adopted on its own; the warm path is an optimisation.

hostProbes.summary: Manager and script identity for the about/diagnostics surface
hostProbes.why: Deliberately unprobed and ungranted: Tampermonkey exposes GM_info to a script with no grants, so bare use is correct. Declared here so nobody 'fixes' it by adding a grant - the grant-equality test would then fail on a permission that buys nothing.

hostProbes.summary: Compositor-side accent flash and the transform transition
hostProbes.why: flashElement() returns early and the settings/toast flash is simply skipped, and the transform path falls back to its rAF setter - both are cosmetic, so no version floor is claimed.
hostProbes.note: Two guarded call sites, one degradation story: the first has no fallback (nothing flashes), the second has an rAF one. getAnimations()/effect.getKeyframes() are optional-chained or typeof-guarded inside the same pass.

hostProbes.summary: Skips a parked video whose opacity or visibility is already collapsed
hostProbes.why: Falls through to the rect-only path below it, so the candidate scan still works; only the cheap reject is lost.

hostProbes.summary: Full-rate pointer sampling for the forge scrub gesture
hostProbes.why: The single event's coordinates are used instead, so a fast drag samples less densely - the gesture stays correct, just coarser.

hostProbes.summary: Predicts the pointer type a touch is becoming, to pick the drag affordance early
hostProbes.why: Nothing is lost on the target: Gecko does not implement it, so the shipped path is already the fallback. Recorded so the typeof guard is not mistaken for dead code.
hostProbes.note: Absent on Firefox, like CloseWatcher - the branch exists for hosts that do ship it.

hostProbes.summary: The document-wide fullscreen gate, its transition events, and the exit call
hostProbes.why: The gate is driven by fullscreenchange and only latches from a real fullscreenElement, so a host without the API never sets fs and document.exitFullscreen() is unreachable; entering degrades to the blocked-embed hint.
hostProbes.note: Not machine-visible: entry is a requestFullscreen() on a local element reference, exit is guarded by the fs value rather than a typeof.
